properties.program:
# Animation tab: frames 250, play-mode loop, fps 25 -- ten seconds.
# inputs: upper, lower -- the lengths of the two arms
#
# Nothing here says where the pendulum is at time t: it has to be
# worked out step by step.  The loop runs the equations of motion
# 1000 times, 0.01 s a step, four steps a frame.  Frame k keeps
# stepping for its first 4k passes and then holds still (the mask m),
# so every frame of the film ends up where the pendulum is at its own
# moment.  The Figure works the whole film out once per knob turn, then
# only plays it.
view -4, -3, 4, 3

g  = 9.81
dt = 0.01

# both arms start raised, the upper at 120 and the lower at 150 degrees
# from hanging straight down; the ghost starts 0.01 degrees further out
a1 = radians(120)
a2 = radians(150)
b1 = radians(120.01)
b2 = radians(150)
w1 = 0
w2 = 0
v1 = 0
v2 = 0

# two bobs of equal mass
px = upper * sin(a1) + lower * sin(a2)
py = -upper * cos(a1) - lower * cos(a2)

# the mount
width 0.03
fill "grey"
rect -0.4, 0, 0.8, 0.11
nofill

repeat 1000
  m = step(i, 4 * frame - 1)

  d  = a1 - a2
  n  = 3 - cos(2 * d)
  k  = w2 * w2 * lower + w1 * w1 * upper * cos(d)
  e1 = (-3 * g * sin(a1) - g * sin(a1 - 2 * a2) - 2 * sin(d) * k) / (upper * n)
  e2 = 2 * sin(d) * (2 * w1 * w1 * upper + 2 * g * cos(a1) + w2 * w2 * lower * cos(d)) / (lower * n)
  w1 = w1 + e1 * dt * m
  w2 = w2 + e2 * dt * m
  a1 = a1 + w1 * dt * m
  a2 = a2 + w2 * dt * m

  d  = b1 - b2
  n  = 3 - cos(2 * d)
  k  = v2 * v2 * lower + v1 * v1 * upper * cos(d)
  e1 = (-3 * g * sin(b1) - g * sin(b1 - 2 * b2) - 2 * sin(d) * k) / (upper * n)
  e2 = 2 * sin(d) * (2 * v1 * v1 * upper + 2 * g * cos(b1) + v2 * v2 * lower * cos(d)) / (lower * n)
  v1 = v1 + e1 * dt * m
  v2 = v2 + e2 * dt * m
  b1 = b1 + v1 * dt * m
  b2 = b2 + v2 * dt * m

  # the lower bob's track; the last three seconds, fading.  Dividing by
  # the mask makes the passes a frame has not reached vanish.
  qx = upper * sin(a1) + lower * sin(a2)
  qy = -upper * cos(a1) - lower * cos(a2)
  color 0.1, 0.4, 0.9, clamp((i - 4 * frame + 300) / 300, 0, 1)
  line px / m, py / m, qx / m, qy / m
  px = qx
  py = qy
end

# the ghost, faint
x1 = upper * sin(b1)
y1 = -upper * cos(b1)
color 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5
width 0.04
line 0, 0, x1, y1
line x1, y1, x1 + lower * sin(b2), y1 - lower * cos(b2)

# the pendulum
x1 = upper * sin(a1)
y1 = -upper * cos(a1)
color "black"
line 0, 0, x1, y1
line x1, y1, px, py
fill "orange"
circle x1, y1, 0.11
circle px, py, 0.11
nofill

font 0.27
align "left"
text -3.85, 2.75, "t = %.1f s", 10 * t
text -3.85, 2.4, "arms %.2f and %.2f", upper, lower
color "grey"
text -3.85, -2.8, "grey: started 0.01 deg further out"

properties.text: THE DOUBLE PENDULUM -- a Figure that works out its own motion.  A double pendulum has no formula for where it will be at time t, so the program steps the equations of motion 1000 times in a repeat loop, 0.01 s a step, and every frame of the ten-second film keeps the state it reached at its own moment.  The Figure does that arithmetic once per change and then only plays the result.  The faint grey ghost starts just 0.01 degrees further out: watch it track the pendulum for a few seconds and then go its own way -- that is chaos.  Turn the knobs to set the lengths of the UPPER and LOWER arms (0.3 to 1.5); both arms always start raised, at 120 and 150 degrees.  Every turn works the whole film out again, which takes a moment.  Open the Figure (double-click) to read the program.
